title: Looking for playtesters and suggestions for my anti-colonialist Total War-lite mobile browser pirate strategy game
author: Potential_Ad_7544
selftext:
​

[https://jacktat.itch.io/avast](https://jacktat.itch.io/avast)

"**Avast!** Command your pirate fleets to take down the Empire and liberate the islands."

Hello all, first time posting here and would hugely appreciate any playtesting and suggestions/ideas for improvement.

This game came into my head almost fully formed, all at once, out of the blue while on holiday in Colombia, reading about the pirate history around Cartagena and the (non-pirate) liberator Simón Bolívar.

Since then I've been working through with Claude to turn it into a reality layer by layer over a few months.

Have always adored the Total War games and I still find it wild that we can now turn these dreams into something you can actually play in a way many of us never could have before.

• **Sail** to a beautiful land of tropical islands, exploring your own unique procedurally generated map

• **Raid** Empire trade routes to get cash for upgrades and new ships. Deploy ships and set their orders, then watch it play out through the autobattler.

• **Liberate** the islands - attack Empire ports and watch the two phase bombard/assault combat unfold through discrete events simulation

• **Battle** enemy fleets and defend the liberated lands from reconquest. Develop your own combat strategies through combinations of orders for each ship in your fleet.

• **Upgrade** your ships at friendly liberated ports - take on the superior numbers of the Empire

As an aside, I had a thoroughly great time designing an entire empire-building conquest/expansion engine with tech trees, resources, dependencies, procedurally generated new settlement creation etc... and then making the entire game be about tearing the whole thing down.

Hugely appreciate in advance any ideas or suggestions for improvement
